_doc: Riverfront fragment for the Point Pleasant case: the district, the floodgate, three witnesses on the river side, the night-3 roost at the Silver Bridge approach, and the evidence the riverbank gives up. Ids are prefixed rf_.

floodgate.name: The floodgate
floodgate.locked: The floodgate is shut for the night. Through the bars, the river, and a sign: SHUT AT DUSK BY ORDER.

facts.title: Lights on the water, 1966

gates.prompt: You've worked this river a long time. What did you see in '66?

lines: November '66, night tow, downbound under the bridge. Two red lights on the water ahead of us, low, where a boat would be.
No bow light, no stern light, and they were moving against the current. Nothing moves against this current without a diesel, and I'd have heard a diesel.
Two lights, low on the water, upstream. Write it down exactly like that.

facts.title: The Belle's radio, December 1967
lines: Channel 16, the afternoon of the fifteenth. Three notes, over and over, for an hour. Skipper said it was Gallipolis testing something. Then the bridge went.
Same interval. Half a step lower. It's the same signal.

facts.title: The run to Gallipolis

gates.prompt: The Belle crosses every morning. Nobody would notice four more.

lines: First light, every day, we cross for the Ohio-side mail and a crewman. You stand on the barge and you don't touch anything.
You miss first light, you wait for tomorrow. The river doesn't do afternoons.

facts.title: The search parties of 1966

gates.prompt: That photo on the wall. You were there?
Towns like this always send men out with lanterns. Who went?

lines: I was fourteen and I carried the lanterns. Two nights on the point after the Register ran it. Twenty men, one dog, and my daddy's shotgun.
Found crane tracks on the bank, big ones, and shot at nothing for two nights. Then the deputy said crane and everybody went home relieved.
Relieved. That's the word I'd have used.

facts.title: No cranes in November

gates.prompt: You know every bird on this river. When do the cranes come through?

lines: Sandhills pass over in March and again in October, high up, and you hear 'em before you see 'em. Never on the ground here. Never in November.
There weren't any in '66 and there aren't any now. I told the deputy that in '66. He bought shells and didn't listen.
So the lab says crane and the one person who'd know says no crane.
I say no crane. I don't say what.

facts.title: Two men bought waders
lines: Them. Tuesday. Two pair of waders, size large, and they asked which way the current ran. Which way the current ran.
Paid in new bills so flat they stuck together. Asked if the pump house was manned at night. I said ask the county.

facts.title: The catfish that pulled a boat
lines: Summer of '71 my cousin Dewey hooked something off this pier that towed his johnboat to the Ohio side and back, twice, and then let go.
Flathead cat. Big as a sofa. Dewey saw its whiskers, says they was long as your arm. Dewey'd had a few, but the boat was wet on the Ohio side, you can't argue a wet boat.
Flatheads top out around a hundred pounds.

facts.title: What the foam is

gates.prompt: That foam by the outfall. You've seen it before.
The glow is strongest where the warm water comes out. Why would that be?

lines: Pump house outfall. The county runs the pumps Thursdays and the foam glows Thursday nights and the fish don't care.
Been doing it since the plant. Your bird don't make soap suds, son.

rf_crane_feather.title: The feather at the point
rf_crane_feather.text: A thirty-centimetre grey feather planted quill-down in the frozen mud below the point.

rf_crane_feather_lab.title: Lab: the point feather
rf_crane_feather_lab.text: Sandhill crane primary, by structure. Thirty centimetres: a third longer than any crane in the key. Crane, and not a crane.

rf_feather_photo.title: Photo of the feather
rf_feather_photo.text: A grey feather in the mud at the point. Could be a crane's. Could be a big crane's.

rf_bank_prints_cast.title: Cast of the point prints
rf_bank_prints_cast.text: Three toes, thirty-two centimetres, toes turned in, and a stride of nearly two metres out of the water and up the bank. No crane walks like that.

rf_bank_prints_photo.title: Photo of the point prints
rf_bank_prints_photo.text: Three-toed prints in frozen mud by the point. A heron. A very big heron.

rf_cold_spot.title: Cold spot, bridge approach
rf_cold_spot.text: Night three: a circle three metres wide on the bridge approach reading twenty degrees below the air, drifting slowly toward the water.

rf_cold_photo.title: Photo of the bridge approach
rf_cold_photo.text: The bridge approach at night. The frame is fogged in a perfect circle. The rest is sharp.

rf_bridge_tone_tape.title: Tape: the plaque, night three
rf_bridge_tone_tape.text: Three notes from the memorial plaque, recorded on the bridge approach. The same three June taped at igloo 7, a half-step lower, and in the bronze you can feel it.

rf_foam_sample.title: Glowing foam
rf_foam_sample.text: Blue-green foam from the river beside the pump house outfall. It glows when the water moves it.

rf_foam_lab.title: Lab: river foam
rf_foam_lab.text: Phosphate runoff and detergent from the pump house outfall. It glows under the lamp. It would glow in a sink.

rf_foam_outfall.title: Chalmer on the foam
rf_foam_outfall.text: The foam glows every Thursday night when the county runs the pumps. It has done so since the plant.

rf_gauge_chart_doc.title: Gauge chart, 15 Dec 1967
rf_gauge_chart_doc.text: The pump house river gauge: flat all afternoon, three even jumps at 4:58, off the paper at 5:04 when the bridge fell.

rf_gauge_chart_photo.title: Photo of the gauge chart
rf_gauge_chart_photo.text: A strip chart dated 15 Dec 1967 with three spikes before the big one.

rf_lights_1966.title: Lights on the water, 1966
rf_lights_1966.text: Two red lights low on the Ohio below the bridge, November 1966, moving against the current with no boat and no engine.

rf_towboat_radio.title: The Belle's radio, 1967
rf_towboat_radio.text: The towboat's VHF took three notes on channel 16 for an hour on the afternoon of 15 December 1967, until the bridge fell.

rf_ferry_run.title: The run to Gallipolis
rf_ferry_run.text: The Kanawha Belle crosses to Gallipolis at first light. Lyle will take you if you stand on the barge and touch nothing.

rf_cable_birds.title: The birds on the cable
rf_cable_birds.text: A woman Lyle pulled from the river in 1967 asked him whether the birds were still on the bridge cable. There had been no birds.

rf_search_parties.title: The 1966 search parties
rf_search_parties.text: Twenty men searched the point for two nights in November 1966, found crane tracks, and went home relieved when the deputy said crane.

rf_crane_season.title: No cranes in November
rf_crane_season.text: Opal Thacker has watched this river for thirty years: sandhills pass in March and October, high, and never land. None in 1966. None now.

rf_suits_waders.title: The suits bought waders
rf_suits_waders.text: Two men in black suits bought waders at the bait shop on Tuesday, asked which way the current ran, and whether the pump house was manned at night.

rf_catfish_tale.title: The catfish that pulled a boat
rf_catfish_tale.text: Chalmer's cousin Dewey was towed to Ohio and back by a flathead catfish the size of a sofa in 1971. The boat was wet.

rf_crane_walk.title: The crane that walks like a man
rf_crane_walk.prompt: The biologist says crane. The cast says a two-metre stride with the toes turned in. What walked your bank, Opal?
